f.title: Definition: adverse drug reaction (RAM), including any reaction where a causal relationship is a reasonable possibility before approval
f.statement: An adverse drug reaction (RAM) is a noxious and unintended response to a medicinal product related to any dose. In pre-approval clinical experience of a new medicinal product or its new uses, particularly when the therapeutic dose cannot be established, any reaction for which a causal relationship between the product and an adverse event is a reasonable possibility (the relationship cannot be ruled out) must be considered an adverse drug reaction.

f.title: Definition: serious and unexpected adverse drug reaction (RAMSI) assessed against the MPI
f.statement: A serious and unexpected adverse drug reaction (RAMSI) is an adverse reaction that results in death, is life-threatening, requires hospitalisation or prolongation of existing hospitalisation, or results in persistent or significant disability or incapacity, and whose nature or severity is not consistent with the product information described in the MPI (Investigator's Brochure) or other documentation.
